question: The inputs are unquantified paired-end FASTQ files (6 samples, 3 treated vs 3 control, human liver), but this environment has no read aligner or pseudo-aligner and no transcriptome/genome index — so the reads cannot be turned into a count matrix here. Can you either (a) provide a gene-level count matrix (or transcript-level abundance files, e.g. salmon/kallisto output) for these 6 samples, or (b) have a quantification-capable resource provisioned — an aligner/quantifier (salmon, kallisto, STAR, HISAT2, or Rsubread) plus a human GRCh38 transcriptome FASTA or prebuilt index?

input.questionContext:
Verified against the environment before asking:
- Package census (names check): salmon, kallisto, STAR, HISAT2, bowtie2, fastp, fastqc, multiqc, cutadapt, RSEM, subread/featureCounts, seqkit, samtools, Rsubread, Rbowtie2, Rhisat2, QuasR, Rfastp, tximport are ALL absent. The CLI track is empty (0 packages). Present read-handling packages (ShortRead, Biostrings, Rsamtools, GenomicAlignments, systemPipeR) can read/QC FASTQ and parse BAM, but none can align or pseudo-align reads, and systemPipeR only orchestrates external command-line aligners that are not installed. Nothing installs at runtime.
- Reference census: /mnt/refs holds GENCODE v50 human GTF annotation and hg38 chrom sizes, but NO genome or transcriptome FASTA usable for indexing (the only FASTA is a PharmCAT GRCh38 genome tar, and there is no aligner to index it with anyway) and no prebuilt salmon/kallisto/STAR/HISAT2 index.

Consequence: the requested contrast (3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch) is fully plannable with DESeq2/edgeR/limma-voom plus Reactome/WikiPathways/MSigDB gene sets that ARE present — but only once counts exist. Every step of the plan would be blocked at step one on quantification, so I am asking rather than submitting a plan whose first step can only report failure.

Also worth flagging for interpretation regardless of route: n=3 vs n=3 is the minimum viable design for DESeq2; dispersion estimates will be imprecise and only large, consistent effects will clear FDR correction.
